spam_recall.question: On the holdout, spam recall is the fraction of true spam messages that the model labels spam. Return that recall. Do not return precision.
spam_recall.reference:
lift = []
for w in vocab:
    ps = (word_counts["spam"][w] + ALPHA) / totals["spam"]
    ph = (word_counts["ham"][w] + ALPHA) / totals["ham"]
    s = word_counts["spam"][w]; h = word_counts["ham"][w]
    if s + h >= 10:
        lift.append((w, math.log(ps/ph), s, h))
lift.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])

rec = sum(1 for g, p in zip(gold, preds) if g == "spam" and p == "spam") / sum(1 for g in gold if g == "spam")
rec = round(rec, 4)

ham_precision.question: Ham precision is the fraction of messages labeled ham that really are ham. Return that precision. Do not return spam recall.
ham_precision.reference:
preds = [classify(t) for _, t in test]
gold  = [l for l, _ in test]
acc = sum(p == g for p, g in zip(preds, gold)) / len(gold)

hp = sum(1 for g, p in zip(gold, preds) if g == "ham" and p == "ham") / sum(1 for p in preds if p == "ham")
hp = round(hp, 4)

cases.input: Ten messages labeled ham and nine are truly ham.
cases.expect: Precision is 9 of 10 ham labels that are correct, not recall.

p_free_spam.question: On the test set, look only at spam messages. What fraction of them contain the word free? Return the probability of free given spam, not given ham.
p_free_spam.reference:
free_test = [(t, g) for (g, t) in test if "free" in t.lower()]
n_free = len(free_test)
n_ham = sum(1 for _, g in free_test if g == "ham")
example = next(t for t, g in free_test if g == "ham")
# e.g. "When you get free, call me" / "Now am free call me pa."

n_spam = sum(1 for g in gold if g == "spam")
n_ham = sum(1 for g in gold if g == "ham")
p_fs = round(sum(1 for _, g in free_test if g == "spam") / n_spam, 4)
p_fh = round(n_ham and sum(1 for _, g in free_test if g == "ham") / n_ham, 4)
p_free_spam = p_fs

cases.input: Half of the spam messages contain the word free.
cases.expect: The probability is free given spam, not free given ham.
